description:
FILED s469bg (Opus, 2026-09-04) while measuring #1035 step 3.

WHAT HAPPENED.  `perl tools/bench-emission-ab.pl --ref c80b1a0 PROG.pl N`
answered

    emission: DIFFERENT
    bench-emission-ab: OUTPUTS DIFFER -- not timed
      A: 190728
      B:

The B side produced NOTHING, and the reason is in the tool's own design note:
it builds ONE saved core, from THIS tree's runtime, and times both emissions
against it -- deliberately, because a per-tree core carries an offset that a
busy box makes large (#995: a byte-identical control row read -8% across trees
while the row under test read -26%).  #1035 step 3 changed `p-sub`'s LAMBDA
LIST (a facts plist at a fixed position after the lambda list), so the BASE
tree's plist-less `p-sub` binds its `facts` parameter to the first body form on
this tree's runtime and the program dies before printing.

WHY IT MATTERS.  This is not a one-off: every future change that alters a
runtime MACRO'S SIGNATURE -- which is what an IR vocabulary change IS -- hits
the same wall, and the tool's message ("OUTPUTS DIFFER -- not timed") points at
the program's output rather than at the cause.  An agent who does not know the
runtime changed will look for a bug in the program.

TWO THINGS TO DO, in order:
 1. CHEAP AND MANDATORY: when the B side produces NO output at all and its
    stderr carries a macroexpansion/arity error naming a `p-*` macro, say so:
    "the base emission does not load on THIS tree's runtime -- a macro
    signature changed; a per-tree comparison is needed".  A diagnosis, not a
    symptom.
 2. OPTIONAL, and it needs a design: a `--two-cores` mode that builds a core
    per tree and reports the per-tree offset EXPLICITLY, by timing a
    byte-identical control program on both cores first and printing that
    spread beside the row's.  The s469bg stand-in
    (`scratch/s469bg/ab-run.sh` in that worktree) is the crude version: it
    times `./runpcl` on each tree, K rounds interleaved, and reports the base
    series' own spread as the control.  Measured there: sub-call-heavy base
    median 1.50 s / new 1.55 s with the base series spanning 1.39-1.66 (19%);
    loop 0.49 / 0.51 against 0.47-0.51 (8%).  Both rows inside their control.

WHAT REPLACED IT AT #1035, and is arguably stronger for this class of change:
MACROEXPANSION EQUALITY.  A `p-let` entry with facts, a classed
`p-raw-params` entry and a `p-sub` with a plist expand to exactly the forms
their bare twins do (`macroexpand-1` EQUAL, four rows in
`Pl/t/decl-facts-01.t`).  When the compiled S-expression is provably the same,
there is nothing left to time -- so a note in the tool pointing at that as the
right bar for an ANNOTATION-only change would be worth as much as the mode.

SCOPE: tools/ only (USER s413: the runners may be replaced, they are not the
product).  Sized as a filler.
subject: tools/bench-emission-ab.pl cannot time a change to a RUNTIME MACRO'S LAMBDA LIST -- it times two emissions on ONE core, so the older emission does not load; give it a second-core mode, or make it say WHY it cannot answer instead of "OUTPUTS DIFFER"
